## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

You can now stop an active run from Discord with `/fro-bot cancel`, targeting it from the run thread or its bound channel. The command reports whether cancellation succeeded and posts a notice in the thread; it avoids cancelling quarantined runs, where owned work may still be running. [#2066](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2066) [#2063](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2063)

### Bug fixes

Gateway run ownership updates are now serialized and duplicate snapshots are skipped, preventing concurrent writes from losing to each other with a conditional-store conflict. The terminal write waits for pending ownership updates to drain, while retaining the existing stale-ETag retry as a backstop. [#2059](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2059)

Discord approval and question cards now show deciding actors where Discord renders them correctly: mentions appear in card descriptions instead of titles, and dashboard approvers appear as escaped plain-text logins rather than broken Discord mentions. Existing non-human decisions and mention suppression remain unchanged. [#2057](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2057) [#2061](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2061)

The Hono update includes fixes for middleware bypasses involving mounted paths and wildcard routes, skipped multipart form validation, CSS helper HTML injection, and CSRF checks for hyperlink-auditing requests. [#2062](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2062)

### Operations

The workspace shell-permission documentation now matches the gateway behavior: commands ask only when an operator rule matches, the last matching rule wins, and commands in compound expressions are checked individually. It also provides a working example for selectively prompting on commands such as `rm` and `sudo`. [#2064](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2064)

Renovate post-upgrade jobs now build only the committed Action bundle where needed, skip builds for lint-only and GitHub Actions updates, and avoid fetching the full AWS SDK changelog. This reduces work on update branches while retaining validation of the generated bundle and Renovate command configuration. [#2054](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2054)

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

When the gateway cannot confirm its repository redaction policy, operator repository and run listings now return `503 redaction-policy-unavailable` instead of an empty `200` response that could be mistaken for having no bindings. A last-known-good policy remains available during its grace window, and denied repositories continue to be filtered; the gateway also rechecks availability after reading bindings in case the grace period expires mid-request. Per-run routes retain their generic `404`, and the change requires Operator contract 1.15.0 with the dashboard deployed as a pair. [#2052](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2052)

On OpenCode V2, run summaries were being submitted as synthetic input with `resume: false`, leaving queued inbox rows that could prevent the next run’s shutdown drain from becoming quiet. The V2 summary write and its related client route and deferral plumbing have been removed; summary writing remains V1-only. Older cached databases may still contain queued rows, but this change creates no new ones, and the PR adds a real-binary test that verifies release leaves no undelivered rows and a subsequent run drains successfully. [#2047](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2047)

Tool approvals are now documented as guidance for a cooperating model, not a security boundary: a tool running under the OpenCode server’s uid can access paths outside the intended workspace or answer its own approval request. The deployment guidance instead identifies the workspace container, its uid, and the egress allowlist as the security boundary. [#2042](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2042)

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

On OpenCode V2, an unsolicited `websearch` call could open a provider-configuration prompt and waste a turn; without a configured provider, upstream defaults could also send queries to a third party. The Action now denies `websearch` while continuing to allow `webfetch`, and its permission gate rejects later rules that re-allow the tool.

V2 tool calls now show useful, sanitized arguments in the transcript, including commands, paths, grep patterns and web URLs with credentials and query details removed. Displayed values are capped at 200 characters, and prompts, file contents and edit bodies stay hidden; Code Mode `execute` calls now produce a line for the call and each nested call. [#2038](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2038)

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

OpenCode V2 runs now handle permission decisions without ending the turn: rejected requests give the model clear direction to continue without the denied action, and approval cards show the command or path being approved. The existing shutdown quarantine remains in place for genuinely suspended runs. [#2026](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2026) [#2028](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2028)

Gateway status is more useful during V2 background work and slow drains. Wait reasons now distinguish owned background tasks from completion checks, and drain logs identify active sessions, shells, and queued item types—without logging message or command text—so a stalled drain points to what is blocking it. [#2031](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2031) [#2036](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2036)

For eligible same-repository PR runs, the Action now tells the agent it will push changes, avoiding a futile direct push attempt. When it brokers a commit, it preserves the agent’s sanitized commit message instead of replacing it with a generic one. [#2033](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2033)

The pre-push hook now checks only the generated Action distribution rather than running all package builds and repository-wide lint; lint, type checks, and the full build suite remain covered by CI. [#2030](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2030)

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

The GitHub Action now defaults to a pinned stock OpenCode V2 build, with `latest` resolving to that pin without a network lookup. V2 installs verify recorded digests and fail closed, while explicit V1 pins remain available for rollback; V1 session history is imported before the first V2 prompt, and V2 writes to separate cache and S3 keys. The first run fails before prompting or saving if that bounded import cannot complete.

The change also updates V2 setup expectations: `auth-json` accepts API-key entries, and Action-managed permission settings are stripped from `opencode-config`. Runtime diagnostics now bound and re-issue session-wait calls, log polling fallback only on errors, and record a single release-verdict line. The wiki documents the separate V1/V2 execution paths and the Action's default switch, including that the workspace image retains its independent V1 default. [#2024](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2024) [#2023](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2023)
